Ibn Abi Dawud mentioned in his tafsir, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the angels entered upon Lot, he thought they were guests who had come to him, so he made a fuss over them and was eager to honour them. But his wife went against him and informed the wicked people of his folk that he had hosted handsome young men, the most beautiful of people in face, the most radiant in beauty, and the most fragrant in scent. That was her betrayal which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His Book.

In the same work, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, regarding His saying ﴿So they betrayed them﴾:

He said: "By Allah, neither of them committed adultery, and the wife of no prophet ever did so." It was then said to him: "What then was the betrayal of the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot?" He replied: "As for the wife of Noah, she used to tell people that he was mad. As for the wife of Lot, she would point out the guests."

(Section)

These verses contain three parables: one parable for the disbelievers, and two parables for the believers.

The parable of the disbelievers includes the fact that the disbeliever is punished for his disbelief and his enmity towards Allah, His Messenger and His allies, and that no kinship by blood, no marital relation, and no other means of connection with the believers will benefit him along with his disbelief.

For all means will be severed on the Day of Resurrection, except what was connected to Allah alone through His messengers. If the bond of kinship, marriage or wedlock could benefit without faith, then the bond that existed between Lot and Noah and their wives would have benefited them. But since the two of them did not avail them anything against Allah, ﴿And it was said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter."﴾ [At-Tahrim: 10]

The verse then cut off the hope of one who commits disobedience to Allah and opposes His command, and who hopes that the righteousness of another, whether a relative or a stranger, will benefit him, even if the two of them had the strongest connection in this world. There is no connection stronger than the connection of sonship, fatherhood and marriage. Noah did not avail his son, nor Abraham his father, nor Noah or Lot their wives, anything against Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate between you﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah: 3].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿The Day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul﴾ [Al-Infitar: 19].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will compensate for another at all﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 48].

And He said: ﴿And fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Luqman: 33].

All of this is a refutation of the false hopes of the polytheists, that those they relied upon besides Allah, whether relatives, in-laws, spouses or companions, would benefit them on the Day of Resurrection, or protect them from the punishment of Allah, or intercede for them with Allah. This is the root of the misguidance and polytheism of the children of Adam, and it is the shirk that Allah does not forgive. It is the very thing for the abolition of which Allah sent all His messengers, revealed all His books, and for opposing whose adherents they waged war and showed enmity.

(Subtlety)

His saying ﴿And it was said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter"﴾

It is as if the whole universe spoke this and said it to them.

(Benefit)

"And Allah has set forth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said: 'My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise'" (66:11). She asked that the house be with Him before she asked that it be in Paradise, for the neighbour comes before the dwelling.

(Section)

As for the two examples given for the believers, the first is the wife of Pharaoh. The point of the example is that a believer's connection to a disbeliever does not harm him at all when he has separated from him in his disbelief and his deeds. The sin of another does not harm the obedient believer in the Hereafter, though he may be harmed by it in this world through the punishment that befalls the people of the earth when they neglect the command of Allah, for it comes upon everyone. Thus her connection to him did not harm the wife of Pharaoh, though he was among the greatest of disbelievers. And the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them, though they were two messengers of the Lord of the worlds.

The second example for the believers is Mary, who had no husband, neither a believer nor a disbeliever. He mentioned three categories of women: the disbelieving woman who has a tie to a righteous man; the righteous woman who has a tie to a disbelieving man; and the unmarried woman with no tie between her and anyone. The first's tie and its cause do not benefit her; the second's tie and its cause do not harm her; and the third's lack of a tie does not harm her in any way.

Then in these examples there are wondrous secrets that suit the context of the surah, for it was revealed in mention of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and a warning against their banding together against him, and that if they do not obey Allah and His Messenger and desire the Hereafter, their connection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will not benefit them, just as the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them. For this reason, the example in this surah concerns the tie of marriage rather than kinship.

Yahya ibn Salam said: Allah set forth the first example warning Aisha and Hafsa, then He set forth the second example for them, urging them to hold fast to obedience.

(Chapter)

In citing Maryam as an example for the believers there is also another lesson: the slander that the enemies of Allah, the Jews, directed at her, and their attributing to her and her son what Allah had cleared them of, did not harm her in the sight of Allah in any way, even though she was the greatest truthful one (al-Siddiqah al-Kubra), chosen above the women of the worlds. Thus the disparagement of the wicked and the corrupt does not harm a righteous man.

In this there is also consolation for ʿĀ'ishah, Mother of the Believers, if the surah was revealed after the incident of the slander (al-ifk), and a reassurance of her soul concerning what the liars said about her, if it was revealed before it. Likewise, in the mention of the example of the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot there is a warning to her and to Ḥafṣah regarding what the two of them had colluded upon concerning the Prophet ﷺ.

These examples thus contain a warning to them, a frightening admonition, an exhortation to them toward obedience and monotheism, and consolation and steadying of the soul for whoever among them was harmed and falsely accused.

The secrets of the revelation are beyond this and greater than it, especially the secrets of the examples, which none understands except those of knowledge.
